hints.text: Equivalent expressions always give the same value. Rewriting one of them can show whether they match.
Expand $2(x + 3)$ by multiplying $2$ by each term inside. Compare what you get with $2x + 6$.
$2(x + 3) = 2x + 6$, the same as the first expression, so the answer is yes.

explanation: Use the distributive property on the second expression, $2(x + 3)$.
Multiplying the $2$ by each term inside gives $2 \cdot x + 2 \cdot 3 = 2x + 6$.
That is exactly the first expression, so the two are equivalent. The answer is yes.
